title: The moon inside
hookLine: after a hard shift, a moon over the parking lot and Kabir's line: the moon shines in my body
tomorrow: they fought over Kabir's body. what was under the sheet?

lines: THE MOON SHINES IN MY BODY.
cards: A patient yelled at Zoe across the clinic desk today, over a referral that wasn't her fault. She kept her voice steady until the shift ended. Then she sat on Ray's porch steps while the moon came up over the parking lot.

Ray, who taught philosophy for years, went inside and came back with a worn book of Kabir, open to this line, in Tagore's English: "The moon shines in my body, but my blind eyes cannot see it." Why can't Kabir see it?
Because his eyes are busy looking out.

teach.h: THE MOON WITHIN, AND THE SUN.
teach.b: The song goes on: the moon is within me, and so is the sun. Kabir isn't boasting about himself.
He's saying what's in every body, and he says it plainest in a hymn kept in the Sikh scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, in the morning raga called Prabhati.
In the first, he sings, God made the light, the noor, and from that light came all people. From one light the whole world welled up.

teach.h: SO WHO IS GOOD, AND WHO IS BAD?
teach.b: So who is good, and who is bad? Don't be fooled, he tells his listeners. That's the teaching: one light in every body.

It runs under Kabir's refusal to rank people by caste or by Hindu and Muslim, and the Sikh scripture keeps this hymn among the Gurus' own. Now bring it back to the desk. Kabir doesn't say the man who yelled behaved well.

teach.h: THE SAME LIGHT IN THE ONE WHO YELLED.
teach.b: He says the same light is in him, even when his eyes, and Zoe's, are too blind to see it. That's harder than calming down. Zoe can still ask him to stop shouting.
By Kabir's hymn, she just doesn't get to decide he's empty inside.
The moon over the parking lot doesn't choose whom it shines on, and Kabir says the one inside doesn't either.

how: Sikhs sing Kabir's hymn of one light ('first, God made the light') in kirtan from the Guru Granth Sahib; in the sant tradition, turning attention inward to the light and sound within is a form of meditation.

o: Kabir's picture of the light in every body
the moon goddess worshiped in Kabir's village
a festival lamp lit at the full moon

games.q: the light in the songs: tap the pairs.
p: can't see the moon in the body
the light God made in the first
the morning raga of Kabir's hymn

s: Kabir means only holy people carry the light inside
from one light came all people. so who is good, and who is bad?
Kabir's hymn of one light is kept in the Guru Granth Sahib
it sits in the morning raga, Prabhati.
seeing the light in someone means you can't ask them to stop
the light is there even in the one who yells; you just don't get to call him empty.

games.q: a neighbor's dog barks all night and the owner shrugs. you're furious. what does Kabir's hymn ask of you?
o: nothing; Kabir's light is only for gentle people
say nothing at all, since everyone carries light
speak up, without deciding the owner is empty inside
games.why: one light in every body doesn't mean silence. it means you can't write anyone off as dark.

practice: Close your eyes and let them rest from looking out. Notice what's behind the lids: dark, a faint glow, a drifting shape. Don't hunt for a moon; just stay with what's there, and let the breath come and go on its own.

wordCard.voice: The moon inside: Kabir's picture of the light in every body, there even when the eyes are too busy to see it.

orig.note: Arabic and Persian: light. Kabir's hymn in the Granth uses it: first, God made the light.

carryVoice: For the road: the moon inside. In the man at the desk too. Five days with the weaver.
